claims.text: A Pulumi blog post titled "SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi" exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/
AWS CDK ties infrastructure to AWS only and does not support multi-cloud (CDK is AWS-only).
AWS CDK supports defining infrastructure only in TypeScript or Python.
Pulumi supports any programming language (table) / TypeScript, Python, Go, or C# (CTA).
Pulumi deployments are faster than AWS CDK deployments because CloudFormation is slower than direct execution.
AWS CDK uses a CloudFormation state file while Pulumi uses Pulumi-managed state.
AWS CDK secrets management is limited to AWS Secrets Manager only.
Pulumi supports AWS, Azure, GCP, and on-prem.
CDK and CloudFormation generate an intermediary format (YAML or JSON) that is then executed to deploy resources.
Pulumi executes infrastructure code directly during deployment rather than generating an intermediary format.

A Founding Engineer at SST said: "With Pulumi, the deployment process feels like a natural extension of writing code - it's intuitive and powerful and capable of advanced things that traditional IaC tools can't handle."
Pulumi Insights product page provides improved visibility and debugging capabilities.
Pulumi has built-in extensibility features such as custom providers and dynamic components.
Ion is the code name for a new SST engine that deploys components using Pulumi instead of CDK and CloudFormation; once stable it will be released as SST v3.
SST uses Pulumi for its providers and deployment engine and bridges Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and includes a free tier.
Pulumi Crosswalk for AWS simplifies day one tasks, documented in the AWS guide at /docs/iac/guides/clouds/aws/.
Pulumi Cloud Deployments docs exist at /docs/pulumi-cloud/deployments/.
Pulumi lets SST offer a faster, more flexible, and provider-agnostic infrastructure experience.
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` requires no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account; the Pulumi engine ships inside the SST CLI.
SST keeps deployment state in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account, not Pulumi Cloud.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, for deploying to AWS and more than 150 other providers.
Through 2023 SST's provisioning layer was built on AWS CDK and CloudFormation; in late 2023 the team began a rewrite code-named Ion.
Ion shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: 'Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications. The constructs (or components) are defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi; as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation (CFN).'
SST's 'Moving away from CDK' blog post says that when you run `sst deploy`, resources call an embedded Pulumi engine that calls their bridged Terraform provider, which makes AWS SDK calls.
SST docs 'What is SST' say: 'SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for the providers and the deployment engine. And Terraform's providers are bridged through Pulumi.'
Gautier Blandin's article states SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka's dev.to article says: 'You may notice right away the imports from Pulumi. It means the whole deployment process will be built on Pulumi now.'

SST's platform package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi, first-party Pulumi providers for AWS, Cloudflare, Docker builds and others, and a Pulumiverse Vercel provider (@pulumi/aws, cloudflare, command, docker-build, random, tls, @pulumiverse/vercel).
The SST repository is at anomalyco/sst (formerly sst/sst) with platform/package.json on the dev branch.
The Pulumi engine diffs desired vs actual state, builds a dependency graph, and orders operations.
Pulumi's Terraform bridge (pulumi-terraform-bridge) is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's engine does not require a Pulumi account, network call to Pulumi Cloud, or any Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API lets teams embed Pulumi programs inside their own tools, and the provider bridge lets Pulumi users consume Terraform providers directly.
AWS alone exposes hundreds of resource types.
Nitric's docs state 'all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments,' with official Nitric providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Defang's pulumi-defang provider takes a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs `pulumi up`; Defang deploys Docker Compose applications to the cloud.
Nitric and Defang run application deployments through the Pulumi engine rather than building their own diff, state, and provider layer.
Resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly in Pulumi and deployed as part of the same SST app.
SST does not invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The sst npm package had roughly 796,000 (796,291) weekly downloads for the week of September 5-11, 2026.
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent, which now has more GitHub stars than SST.
opencode is an AI coding agent, opencode.ai, whose team overlaps with SST's.
Anyone running SST is running Pulumi's engine.
Pulumi Cloud, policy as code, and components provide cross-team visibility, central guardrails, and sharing of infrastructure patterns, and can be used with the same engine SST uses.
The team's broadened attention to opencode hasn't changed SST's release cadence or its dependency on the Pulumi engine.
SST is a strong fit for opinionated full-stack applications; Pulumi directly is better for cross-team visibility, policy enforcement, or infra shared across applications.
Linked pages exist: /blog/aws-cdk-vs-pulumi-why-sst-switched/, /docs/iac/guides/basics/how-pulumi-works/, /blog/any-terraform-provider/, /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/, and others.
